variant_hint.yorker: Full at the toes. Deadly when perfect, a full toss when loose.
variant_hint.good_length: The honest stock ball. Seams on a green pitch.
variant_hint.bouncer: Short and rising. Hurries batters on a hard pitch.
variant_hint.slower: Disguised pace that beats an early swing. Grips on a slow pitch.
variant_hint.inswing: Curves into the pads, hunting LBW and bowled.
variant_hint.outswing: Curves away from the bat, hunting an edge to the slips.
variant_hint.offspin: Turns into the batter. Grips on a slow pitch.
variant_hint.legspin: Turns away for edges and stumpings. Risky when loose.
intent_hint.attack: Hunts wickets, but leaks more boundaries.
intent_hint.contain: Dries up runs. Takes fewer wickets.
intent_hint.setup: A sighter that makes your next attacking ball deadlier.
field_hint.attacking: Slips and close catchers. Gaps at third man and fine leg.
field_hint.balanced: A ring that saves singles. Gaps at mid-off and midwicket.
field_hint.sweeper: Boundary riders stop fours. Mid-on is open.
shot_hint.defend: Block it. The safest shot, rarely a run.
shot_hint.rotate: Push into a gap for one or two. Low risk.
shot_hint.drive: Front foot, full balls, along the ground.
shot_hint.cut_pull: Back foot, short or wide balls, hit square.
shot_hint.sweep: Down on one knee to spin and full balls.
shot_hint.loft: In the air for four or six. Needs the right length.
shot_hint.leave: Let it go. Safe outside off, risky on the stumps.
pitch_hint.green: Seam and swing. Edges carry to the slips.
pitch_hint.hard: Pace and bounce. Timed shots race away.
pitch_hint.slow: Spin and slower balls grip. Keep it on the ground.
ghost.anchor.name: The Anchor
ghost.anchor.style: Tidy overs and patient batting. The friendliest ghost to start with.
ghost.swinger.name: The Swinger
ghost.swinger.style: Swings it both ways with catchers waiting, and loves a cover drive.
ghost.enforcer.name: The Enforcer
ghost.enforcer.style: Bouncers and yorkers to a sweeper field. Swings hard at everything.
ghost.trickster.name: The Trickster
ghost.trickster.style: Spin, slower balls and sneaky set-ups. Sweeps and finds the gaps.
ghost.maestro.name: The Maestro
ghost.maestro.style: The right plan for every pitch. Reads your field like a book.
advice.unlock.slower: Unlock: keep a batter to 6 runs or fewer in your over
advice.unlock.inswing: Unlock: hit the stumps (bowled or LBW)
advice.unlock.legspin: Unlock: take a wicket with off-spin
advice.unlock.where: You earn these in Friend Duels and Group Cups. They can never be bought.
advice.pitch.green: Green pitch: seam and swing on a good length work best, most of all in the first three balls. Spin is easier to hit.
advice.pitch.hard: Hard pitch: yorkers and bouncers bite. A full ball that isn't a yorker is easy to smash.
advice.pitch.slow: Slow pitch: spin and slower balls grip. Fast short balls and full swing sit up to be hit.
advice.weather.humid: Humid air: the ball swings more.
advice.weather.dew: Dew: the ball is wet and hard to grip, so batting is easier. Spinners suffer most.

advice.read.attack: All-out attack: more wickets, but more fours and sixes too.
advice.read.contain: Playing it safe: fewer fours, but fewer wickets too.
advice.read.energy_left: {n} energy left over. A faster or trickier ball could use it.
explain.yorker_vs_defend: Bat jammed down on the yorker: safe, but hard to score.
explain.yorker_vs_rotate: Squeezing a yorker away for a run is the safe, smart answer.
explain.yorker_vs_drive: Driving a yorker needs perfect timing: it's right at the toes.
explain.yorker_vs_cut_pull: There is nothing to cut or pull when the ball is at your toes.
explain.yorker_vs_sweep: Sweeping a yorker is a gamble with the pads and the stumps.
explain.yorker_vs_loft: No room to get under a yorker: lofts get skied or miss.
explain.good_length_vs_defend: The honest ball met the honest shot.
explain.good_length_vs_rotate: Soft hands into a gap: the safe way to milk a good-length ball.
explain.good_length_vs_drive: The drive loves a full ball and hates a short one: length decided it.
explain.good_length_vs_cut_pull: Cut and pull need the ball short: length decided it.
explain.good_length_vs_sweep: The sweep works on a full ball, not a short one: length decided it.
explain.good_length_vs_loft: Lofting needs a full ball, or a short one to hook. A good length is the hardest to clear.
explain.bouncer_vs_defend: Blocking a bouncer is awkward: it climbs towards the gloves.
explain.bouncer_vs_rotate: A rising bouncer is hard to steer into a gap.
explain.bouncer_vs_drive: Driving a bouncer means reaching for a ball that isn't there.
explain.bouncer_vs_cut_pull: Short and rising: the pull is on when the timing is there.
explain.bouncer_vs_sweep: You can't sweep a ball that's at head height.
explain.bouncer_vs_loft: Hooking a bouncer in the air: six if it's timed, caught if it's top-edged.
explain.slower_vs_defend: Waiting for the slower ball and blocking it: patience, no harm done.
explain.slower_vs_rotate: Soft hands on a slower ball: easy to steer for a run.
explain.slower_vs_drive: A drive at a slower ball has to wait for it: patience pays, haste doesn't.
explain.slower_vs_cut_pull: A short slower ball sits up to be pulled; a full one cramps the cut.
explain.slower_vs_sweep: The sweep takes the slower ball's disguise out of play.
explain.slower_vs_loft: Lofting a slower ball means waiting for it: it's easy to be early.
explain.inswing_vs_defend: A straight bat covers the in-swinger heading for the pads.
explain.inswing_vs_rotate: Working the in-swinger off the pads: going with the swing.
explain.inswing_vs_drive: Drive a full in-swinger straight and it flies; miss it and the pads are in line.
explain.inswing_vs_cut_pull: Cutting an in-swinger means playing against the swing: it cramps you.
explain.inswing_vs_sweep: Sweeping an in-swinger puts the pad in the way: LBW danger.
explain.inswing_vs_loft: Lofting the in-swinger: clear the swing and it flies, miss and the pads are in line.
explain.outswing_vs_defend: Defending the out-swinger: the danger is the edge to the slips.
explain.outswing_vs_rotate: Soft hands guide the out-swinger down towards third man.
explain.outswing_vs_drive: Drive the out-swinger and it can fly through cover, or find the outside edge.
explain.outswing_vs_cut_pull: Width plus swing: the cut is the natural answer.
explain.outswing_vs_sweep: Sweeping a ball that swings away is a reach: hard to control.
explain.outswing_vs_loft: Lofting against away swing: the edge is never far away.
explain.offspin_vs_defend: A firm forward block smothers the off-spin.
explain.offspin_vs_rotate: Off-spin turning in is easy to work into the leg side.
explain.offspin_vs_drive: Driving off-spin means getting to the pitch of the ball.
explain.offspin_vs_cut_pull: Cutting an off-spinner turning in is cramped, unless it's a long hop.
explain.offspin_vs_sweep: The sweep takes the off-spinner's turn out of play.
explain.offspin_vs_loft: Using your feet to off-spin turns it into a full toss, or a stumping.
explain.legspin_vs_defend: Leg-spin turning away from a defensive bat looks for the edge.
explain.legspin_vs_rotate: Leg-spin turning away is tricky to steer into a gap.
explain.legspin_vs_drive: Driving leg-spin: reach the pitch of it, or the turn finds the edge.
explain.legspin_vs_cut_pull: Leg-spin turning away gives room to cut, especially when it's short.
explain.legspin_vs_sweep: Sweeping against the turn of leg-spin is risky.
explain.legspin_vs_loft: Lofting leg-spin: reach the pitch and it sails, miss and you're stumped.
explain.timing_perfect: Perfect timing: the swing came at exactly the right moment.
explain.timing_good: Good timing made the most of the shot.
explain.timing_early: Early: the bat came through before the ball arrived.
explain.timing_late: Late: the ball was on the batter before the bat came down.
explain.timing_very_early: Far too early: the shot was finished before the ball got there.
explain.timing_very_late: Far too late: the ball beat the bat for pace.
explain.no_shot: No swing at all: the ball did the rest.
explain.loose_ball: A loose delivery is a gift: easier to punish.
explain.pinpoint: Pinpoint release: the ball hit its mark and left no room.
explain.pitch_green: The green pitch played its part: it helps seam and swing, not spin.
explain.pitch_hard: The hard pitch played its part: bouncers and yorkers bite, everything else gets hit.
explain.pitch_slow: The slow pitch played its part: spin and slower balls grip, pace sits up.
explain.weather_humid: Humid air gave the swing bowler extra help.
explain.weather_dew: Dew made the ball wet and harder for the bowler to grip.
explain.field_gap: The field left a gap right there.
explain.field_ring: The ring field gave that shot almost no room.
explain.field_deep: A deep fielder was there: easy runs in front, danger for the big hit.
explain.field_packed: That side of the field was packed.
explain.field_slips: It went towards the slips, and the field there decided it.
explain.field_close: Close catchers were crowding the bat.
explain.setup_worked: The ball before set this one up.
explain.repeat_lined_up: Same ball again: the batter had it lined up.
explain.new_batter: First ball for a new batter: the hardest one to face.
explain.against_the_line: Playing across the line of the ball is risky.
explain.leave_safe: Left alone safely: it was never going to hit the stumps.
explain.leave_survived: Left alone, and survived: that one could have hit the stumps.
explain.leave_straight: Leaving a straight ball is dangerous.
explain.unanswered: No answer in time, so the ball counted as a safe leave.
explain.last_ball_scramble: Last-ball scramble: running on anything has a price.
explain.run_out_risk: A quick run straight to a fielder is a risky run.
explain.stumped_charge: Charged the spinner, missed, and the keeper did the rest.
explain.dead_ball: Dead ball: two wickets had already fallen, so this ball didn't count.

guide.title: How to win at Sealed Six
guide.intro: Every match is two tiny innings: you bowl one over and bat against one. Plan smart, time your swipe and outthink your friend.
guide.sealing.title: Sealed overs: no peeking
guide.sealing.body: Before the match you plan your six balls and lock them. Locking seals the plan with a secret code, so nobody can change it or see it, not even you. Your friend does the same. When you have both batted, the overs are unsealed and the whole match plays out. Anyone can check that the codes match, so nobody can cheat.
guide.match.title: How a match works
guide.match.body: Each player bowls one over of six balls and bats against the other player's over. Two wickets and your innings is over, but you still face every ball so nobody can tell. You won't see your runs or wickets until the reveal, only how well you timed each shot. Most runs wins.
guide.energy.title: Energy: you can't bowl only rockets
guide.energy.body: You have 15 energy for your six balls. Spin and good-length balls are cheap; swing, bouncers and slower balls cost more; yorkers cost the most. Each step up in pace costs one more. Six yorkers will never fit, so mix it up. The Super Ball has its own small allowance.
guide.intent.title: Intent: your secret plan for each ball
guide.intent.body: Attack hunts wickets but gives away more boundaries. Contain keeps the runs down but takes fewer wickets. Set up is a quiet ball that makes your next attacking ball deadlier, as long as the two are different: short then full, fast then slow, swinging in then out. The batter never sees your intent.
guide.timing.title: Timing: swipe and let go
guide.timing.body: Pick your shot, then swipe towards where you want to hit it. The moment you lift your finger is your timing: lift it just as the ball arrives for perfect timing. Fast balls give you less time and slow spinners make you wait. Changes of pace are a trap: after a fast ball it's easy to be early on a slow one.
guide.pitches.title: Read the pitch
guide.pitch.green: Green pitch: the grass makes the ball swing and seam, and edges fly to the slips. Seam and swing bowlers love it, especially for the first three balls. Spinners don't.
guide.pitch.hard: Hard pitch: fast and bouncy. Bouncers and yorkers are dangerous, but well-timed shots race to the boundary. Cuts and pulls are strong here.
guide.pitch.slow: Slow pitch: the ball grips and stops. Spinners and slower balls rule; pace and bounce lose their bite. Lofted shots are hard, so keep it on the ground and sweep the spinners.
guide.weather.body: Weather is a small nudge you can always see: humid nights help swing, and dew makes the ball wet so spinners grip less.
guide.super_ball.title: The Super Ball
guide.super_ball.body: When you plan your over you also pick one extra ball: the Super Ball. It's only used if the scores are tied. Each player faces the other's Super Ball, and whoever scores more off it wins.
guide.super_ball.ladder: Still level? Fewer wickets lost wins. Still level? More fours and sixes wins. Still level? It's a tie, and that's rare.
